statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 5 during the 21:00-22:00 UTC CME maintenance halt, when no price path can form and the assessment rests on a verified, orderly, mid-range cash close, while stress holds at 72 on WTI at a six-week $94.25, Brent near $100 and a 10-year at the top of its range.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour. The Nasdaq-100 closed 107 points above its session low after a gradual two-sided fade, and no repeated extension after a failed retracement was observed at any point in the session. Nasdaq-100 futures are in the daily CME maintenance halt, so the current clock-hour carries no price path at all rather than an adverse one. Cross-asset channels are firm but conflicting, which raises stress rather than tail. The narrow flagged window covers the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, the horizon's only genuine liquidity discontinuity before Wednesday's cash open, given an active US-Iran tanker conflict and Brent near $100. Tail remains far below the block threshold across all 24 forecast hours.
headline: NDX closes at 29,507.70, down 0.12% and well off its low, with NQ halted at 29,525.75; WTI at $94.25 and a 4.806% 10-year keep stress at 72 while a two-sided session and the maintenance halt hold tail at 5
body:
The US cash session has closed and Nasdaq-100 futures are inside the CME daily maintenance halt, which runs from 21:00 to 22:00 UTC. The current clock-hour therefore carries no price path at all, which is a market-structure fact rather than an evidence gap, and the assessment rests on verified closing levels. The Nasdaq-100 finished at 29,507.70, down 36.45 points or 0.12%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 day range and just under the 29,544.15 prior close. That close sits 107 points above the session low and 148 points below the high. Nasdaq-100 futures last printed 29,525.75, down 0.13%, inside a 29,425.00 to 29,764.75 range, with the final tick at 20:59:59 UTC immediately before the halt; a second reading from Investing.com shows the same 29,525.75 level, so the reference is corroborated. The path into the close was a gradual, two-sided fade of roughly fifty points per hour off the futures high rather than a directional leg, and at no point in the session was repeated extension after a failed retracement observed. That is the direct opposite of the structure capable of overwhelming a mean-reversion basket, which is why tail eases to 5 during a window in which no price can form at all, even as the surrounding channels stay firm.

Index internals were unusually dispersed, which is why the dominant mode stays mixed rather than trend-down. The Dow closed 628.18 points lower at 52,786.07, a 1.18% decline, the S&P 500 fell 0.58% to 7,673.52, the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.32% to 26,421.41, and the Nasdaq-100 lost only 0.12%. Within the index, semiconductors led decisively while megacaps lagged: Intel gained about 9.0% on reported price increases, AMD about 5.9%, Arm about 3.7%, Qualcomm about 3.2% and Broadcom about 3.0%, against Nvidia down about 2.0% and Micron down about 1.6%. Apple and Microsoft each fell about 1.1%, Amazon 0.6% and Meta 0.5%, while Tesla rose about 3.9%. Application software was the notable weak spot, down roughly 3.5% on renewed concern about AI displacement of software revenue. A market in which the semiconductor complex is bid while megacaps and software are offered is rotating, not trending, and rotation is the environment in which mean reversion works rather than fails.

The cross-asset picture is the reason stress stays in the high band at 72. WTI settled at $94.25, up $2.77 or 3.03%, its highest in six weeks, and Brent reached about $99.46, the highest since 24 July, after Houthi missile and drone strikes set Saudi energy installations alight and forced some operations to halt. Marine analytics cited in current reporting put Strait of Hormuz transits at six to thirteen vessels a day against roughly twenty million barrels a day of pre-war flow, and Goldman Sachs has raised its oil forecasts on an assumption that Middle East shipping disruption persists into 2027. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.806%, up 2.2 basis points and at the top of a 4.760 to 4.812 daily range, with the 2-year at about 4.40%. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20 billion of US goods, at rates from 15% to 50%, took effect just after midnight, and government sources report no active talks. Rate-hike odds for the 15-16 September FOMC meeting were marked at about 58% after the strong August payroll report. Against all of that, the VIX closed at 15.72, up 2.75% inside a 15.22 to 15.94 range, which is firmer on the day but absolutely low and inconsistent with a market pricing a disorderly repricing.

The single flagged window is 21:55 to 22:30 UTC, covering the Globex reopen. It is the horizon's only genuine liquidity discontinuity before Wednesday's cash open: an active tanker conflict and Brent within touching distance of $100 can move a thin book in a way that is difficult to distinguish from a real trend in real time. Nothing about that reopen is observed at the assessment cutoff, and the base case is an orderly restart near the pre-halt reference. Beyond it, Wednesday brings the MBA mortgage print at 11:00 UTC, the Apple product keynote and the US 10-year note auction paired at 17:00 UTC, and the API crude inventory report at 20:30 UTC, before Thursday's PPI and Oracle results and Friday's CPI. Those are checkpoints, not automatic blocks; event importance and surprise magnitude are scored as stress and confidence effects until an observed price path establishes otherwise. Confidence sits at 88. Closing levels, futures, VIX, both Treasury yields, crude, index internals, the verified calendar and current reporting were all obtained and corroborated this hour, and the only missing element, a live NQ price path, is missing because the exchange is closed rather than because the evidence could not be gathered. Shared Finviz cross-asset context collected at 20:20 UTC was consistent with the independently verified picture across index futures, rates, energy, breadth, megacaps and semiconductors, and was used only as confirmation.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the EA_ON band without interruption. Tail ran between 5 and 10 from Monday evening through Tuesday morning, stepped up to 15 in the 14:00 UTC slot on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back through 8, 7 and 6 as that leg was fully retraced, ran at 8 through the power hour and closed the window at 6. Stress climbed steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to 72 in early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect, eased to the high 60s through the afternoon, and firmed back to 72 into the close as crude pressed to six-week highs. Confidence improved monotonically from 75 to 89 as the overnight evidence base was replaced by live cash-session observation. The dominant mode was mixed for almost the entire window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, sat at normal through the quiet Monday evening hours, and turned to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon opens inside the CME daily maintenance halt, where no price path can form, so conditional tail sits at the horizon floor of 5. It steps to 9 at the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, which is the flagged window and the horizon's narrowest genuine discontinuity checkpoint given the active US-Iran tanker conflict and Brent near $100. Conditional tail then settles between 6 and 8 through the Asian session, lifts to 8 at the 07:00 UTC European cash open, and holds in the 7 to 8 range through the European morning and the US pre-market. The horizon peak of 13 falls in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full hour after Wednesday's US cash open, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure capable of overwhelming mean reversion; nothing about that structure is observed, and Tuesday's equivalent slot reached 15 before fully retracing within the hour. Scores then decay through midday before lifting to 10 at the 17:00 UTC pairing of Apple's confirmed product keynote with the US 10-year note auction, and the horizon closes at 8 through Wednesday's cash close. All 24 slots stay inside the EA_ON band. Three unresolved channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy, where the tanker conflict is active and Hormuz transit is heavily constrained; the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect with no talks under way; and rate expectations, with roughly 58% priced for a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting ahead of Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI. Stress stays in the high band throughout because none of those channels resolves inside the horizon, while confidence decays overnight as the close-based evidence set ages and recovers once Wednesday's cash session provides fresh observable structure.
